 LIVE - Live coverage of the Qatar Grand Prix Sprint Race at Lusail
 The Lusail Sprint gets underway at 5:00 p.m. Italian time, with Bezzecchi leading the field after a record-breaking pole position. Marquez starts second, Di Giannantonio third, while Martin will have to fight his way up from eleventh. Crucial World Championship points at stake

 LIVE Ended
 That brings our LIVE coverage of the Sprint Race in Lusail to an end – thank you for following it with us! Stay tuned to GPONe for all the post-race comments from the key players, and don’t forget to tune in to our Bar Sport programme tonight. Stay tuned

 Marc earns a match point
 With this victory, Marc takes his tally to 411 points, 49 points clear of Martín, who put in a truly commendable performance today. Marco Bezzecchi, on the other hand, has lost any chance of winning the title, and there is bound to be some controversy over what happened on the track. 
 --:--

 LAP 10 – FINAL LAP
 Marc Márquez wins the Sprint at Lusail, with Di Giannantonio finishing second ahead of a stoic Martín. Fernández finishes 4th ahead of Zarco, Acosta, Ogura and Bastianini. Lecuona is the last rider to score points.

 LAP 10 – FINAL LAP
 A battle between Diggia and Martìn – neither of them wants to give up!!!!
 --:-- 
 --:-- 
 LAP 10 – FINAL LAP
 Marc begins the final lap in the lead, with a lead of 1'2. Martín is defending his second place tooth and nail. You can tell he’s tired; he’s making a few small mistakes. 
 --:-- 
 --:-- 
 LAP 9
 Marc’s lead has stretched to over a second, whilst Di Giannantonio looks set to challenge Martín and give Marc Márquez a nice present. Meanwhile, Bastianini is closing in on Acosta for sixth place. 
 --:-- 
 --:-- 
 ROUND 8
 Marc Márquez is pulling away from Martín, who is clearly feeling the strain on his right arm. He is now 9 tenths ahead, and Marc is racing towards victory. Di Giannantonio remains in 3rd place ahead of Raúl Fernández, Zarco, Acosta and Bastianini. Ogura is ahead of Moreira, the last rider to score points. 
 --:-- 
 --:-- 
 LAP 7
 Marc is chasing victory ahead of Jorge Martín, who remains about half a second behind. In any case, Jorge is putting in a brilliant performance. Di Giannantonio is third. There will be no consequences following the crash between Márquez and Bezzecchi, which has just been reported. Massimo Rivola is not taking it well in the Aprilia pit. 
 --:-- 
 --:-- 
 LAP 6
 Marc remains in the lead, with Martín now 4 tenths behind Marc. But we’re awaiting a decision regarding Marc’s incident with Bezzecchi, as it could change everything. Di Giannantonio is 3rd ahead of Raúl Fernández, followed by Zarco, Acosta, Bastianini and Ogura.

 ROUND 5
 Martín attacked and overtook Marc Márquez – what a brilliant race! Jorge isn’t giving up. The collision between Márquez and Bezzecchi is under investigation – there could be a few surprises!!!!! Marc’s in the lead, but Jorge isn’t letting him get away.

 LAP 4

 ROUND 3

 ROUND 1
 Second start of the Sprint race, and Marc Márquez is first into the first corner, having got off to a better start than Bezzecchi! Di Giannantonio is 3rd ahead of Zarco, who got off to a brilliant start. Marc has made an incredible start. Raúl Fernández is 5th ahead of Acosta. Martín has fought his way back up to 7th place. 
 Who's fastest right now? Check the live timing 
 --:-- 
 --:-- 
 Warm-up lap
 The drivers are completing their warm-up lap; they will then have to complete the 10 laps of this short-distance Sprint race. 
 --:-- 
 --:-- 
 Double long lap for Aldeguer
 Fermin Aldeguer has been handed a double long-lap penalty for the crash he caused with Bagnaia; we are awaiting news on Bagnaia’s condition from the medical centre. 
 --:-- 
 --:-- 
 Pitlane tightens up
 The pit lane is now open to allow the riders to line up on the grid. There is still no news of Bagnaia.

 --:--

 Bagnaia at the medical centre
 Pecco Bagnaia has been taken to the medical centre. We have no further news at present. It has been confirmed that the incident will be investigated after the Sprint Race. 
 --:--

 5 minutes until the departure procedure
 The start procedure will take place in 5 minutes. The drivers will then line up, followed by a warm-up lap and the start. 
 --:--

 Bagnaia is conscious
 Pecco, as seen on the cameras, is conscious – that’s good news. The race will resume over 10 laps, and there will be a rolling start.

Marquez is second, whilst Bagnaia, who makes a good move, is third ahead of Di Giannantonio. Next come Ogura and Fernandez, whilst Martín remains in 11th.  Martìn will have to hang in there
 Jorge Martín faces his real test. It’s one thing to complete a few-lap runs, quite another to tackle the full race distance.  The stage is set, and this time Aprilia starts ahead of everyone else. The Qatar Grand Prix Sprint Race gets underway at 5:00 p.m. Italian time, 11 laps of the Lusail circuit that could carry enormous weight in the world title race . On one side, Marco Bezzecchi, blisteringly fast since Friday and the man behind an extraordinary pole position. On the other, Marc Marquez, who still has the World Championship in his own hands and could mathematically clinch his tenth world title as early as tomorrow.
 Qualifying confirmed just how competitive Aprilia is in Qatar. Bezzecchi stopped the clock at 1'50"028, setting a new outright lap record and beating Marquez by 266 thousandths . A performance that tells only part of the story of the RS-GP's potential, with the bike also looking very strong on race pace. Marc himself acknowledged the superiority of the rider from Romagna, admitting that Bezzecchi seems to have something extra at the moment.

 Completing the front row will be Fabio Di Giannantonio, third after topping Friday's pre-qualifying. But the real surprise is the number of Aprilias on the first two rows, with Raul Fernandez fourth and Ai Ogura sixth. Francesco Bagnaia will start between them , fifth on a Ducati that seems to have regained its competitiveness after struggling at recent rounds.
 Follow 
 The situation is considerably more complicated for Jorge Martin. The reigning world champion, back on the bike despite the right wrist injury he sustained at Phillip Island, could do no better than the eleventh-fastest time. Starting from the fourth row is a major handicap for the Spaniard, especially in a short race like the Sprint, where gaining positions immediately will be crucial.
 Martin will be one of the riders to watch closely, as his long-distance battle with Marquez could have major consequences for the championship standings. The Ducati rider arrived at Lusail with a 44-point lead over his compatriot and 67 over Bezzecchi . The Sprint will not decide the title just yet, but it could put Marc in the ideal position to seal the deal in Sunday's race.

 Keep an eye, though, on Pedro Acosta too, eighth on the grid after coming through Q1, and above all on the battle between Ducati and Aprilia. The Noale-based manufacturer seems to have everything it takes to disrupt Marquez's plans, but the Spaniard has shown time and again that he can turn even difficult situations into opportunities to score points.

 All this on a weekend still dogged by controversy over the geopolitical situation in Qatar and Yamaha's decision not to take part in the Grand Prix, leaving just 18 riders on the grid. Bezzecchi will try to break away , Marquez will have to decide how much to risk, and Martin faces a difficult fightback.
